newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY PM SAYS COALITION HAS CHANCES TO WIN IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY PM SAYS COALITION HAS CHANCES TO WIN IN 1998.

text.p: Hungary's governing coalition has chances to win parliamentary elections next year, Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Hungarian Radio on Sunday.

"Unless extraordinary, unexpected, unfavourable developments emerge, the coalition has very serious chances to win elections in 1998," Horn said in an interview. "I don't think there would be any extraordinary (developments)."

Hungary's governing coalition is made up of the senior coalition member Socialist Party (MSZP) and of the junior member Alliance of Free Democrats (SZDSZ). They together gained around 53 percent of the popular vote in the 1994 election, giving them 72 percent of seats in Parliament.
The most recent opinion polls put the Socialists ahead.

A poll by Hungarian firm Szazadveg-TARKI made for the daily Magyar Hirlap and published in mid-July, gave the Socialist Party 32 percent while the opposition parties the Federation of Young Democrats (Fidesz) and the Independent Smallholders (FKGP) scored 26 and 21 percent, respectively.

In polls published late June, Gallup gave the Socialists 30 percent, Fidesz 27 percent and FKGP 21 percent, while a poll by Szonda-Ipsos put the Socialist Party ahead with 31 percent, compared to 22 percent for Fidesz and 21 percent for FKGP.
